$comment: AGENTS.md 9: 'Every new sensitive route adds a row to the RBAC permission-matrix fixture. Do not merge a route without updating it.' This is that fixture. It is the per-route answer to three questions the decorators pose: which permission gates the route, what is audited on it, and which licence feature it needs. permission-matrix.spec.ts reconciles this file against the source tree in BOTH directions, so a route added without a row fails the gate and a row left behind by a deleted route fails it too. The route is keyed on METHOD plus path rather than a file and line, because that is the only identifier of a route that survives a refactor.
$schema_note: Enforced by apps/api/src/modules/rbac/permission-matrix.spec.ts, which reads the real source tree through scripts/check-route-guards.mjs. Nothing else validates this file.
permission_enforced_by: PermissionGuard (PLT-201). Registered globally in app.module.ts; honours @Public.
entitlement_enforced_by: NOTHING. @RequireEntitlement is read by no guard in this repository. Epic 03 is the story that will enforce it, so `entitlement` below is a RECORD of intent, not a control.
audit_enforced_by: NOTHING. @Audited writes no row. PLT-402 is the story that will write audit_records. The `audited` column records the key the decorator carries and no more.

routes.notes: The ONLY route in the tree that is permission-gated today, and therefore the only route whose behaviour changes when a role is not granted this key: the caller is refused 403 even with a perfectly valid session. Authentication is separate and still applies — a caller with no session is refused 401 before permissions are consulted, which is the ordering app.module.ts relies on. This route binds a Google identity to the caller's OWN account, which is why it needs a permission and not merely a session.
@Public. A permission check here would require the permission the route exists to obtain. Grants nothing, reads no row, consults no role. Justified in route-guards.allowlist.json.

@Public, and @Audited writes nothing yet. The authorisation on this route is the HMAC-signed state bundle plus the ExternalIdentity lookup, not a role — no account, session or role exists before a verified identity is resolved. Justified in route-guards.allowlist.json.

@Public, and @Audited writes nothing yet. Sign-in is how a session is obtained, so a permission check would require the permission the route exists to grant. Deliberately NO entitlement: a Basic-edition school must still be able to sign in or it cannot use the product at all. Justified in route-guards.allowlist.json.

@Public, and @Audited writes nothing yet. The one-time setup token IS the credential on this route. It is the only unauthenticated WRITE in the system, bounded by the token itself, argon2id and a per-source throttle — all independent of RBAC. Justified in route-guards.allowlist.json.

The route PLT-204 reads its permission set from. Every system role holds PERMISSION_READ_OWN from the first seed (system-roles.ts), so every legitimate account is answered; a role that did not hold it is refused 403 even with a perfectly valid session, which is the direct-API bypass PLT-205 T3 proves over a real socket in permissions-over-http.integration.spec.ts. The account whose set is read is the principal SessionGuard attached — there is no userId parameter, so a caller cannot read another account's set. Not audited: reading one's own permission keys is not a sensitive action under AGENTS.md 2.3's list (no finance, grades, permissions mutation, override, issuance, posting or wallet movement).
